posts:
Haitian meatpacking workers in Colorado face deportation, yet they voted 99% to strike anyway.
Evidence: Labor Dignity, Deportation Threats, Corporate Exploitation
#Aletheia #Labor #Immigration

JBS claims it prioritizes employee safety, follows all laws, and has no substantiated evidence of human trafficking or housing exploitation at its Greeley plant.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Over 1,000 Haitian workers face imminent deportation while enduring dangerous line speeds and predatory housing, forcing a historic strike vote.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.62, -0.57) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
Vulnerable migrants are squeezed between federal deportation threats and corporate exploitation, choosing a high-risk strike over silent abuse.
Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.0, Uncertainty z: 0)

- JBS Labor: FAIL (-0.75, -0.80) — Exploits vulnerable migrants.
- UFCW Strike: COND (0.45, -0.30) — Courageous resistance.

In Greeley, Colorado, Haitian meatpacking workers voted overwhelmingly to strike against JBS, protesting extreme line speeds and alleged human trafficking, even as federal courts threaten their legal status.

The Bright Side:
The strike demonstrates the profound agency and solidarity of migrant workers, refusing to let legal vulnerability strip them of their human dignity.
The breakdown lies in the WHO vs WHAT error. JBS focuses on formal compliance (WHAT), while ignoring the human reality (WHO) of workers trapped in predatory housing and dangerous shifts.

Social Physics Analysis:
JBS executes a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using the workers' legal vulnerability as leverage to run high-speed lines while projecting blame onto external recruiters. The workers break this loop through a Smart Altruistic Coalition.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between corporate safety claims and the reality of predatory exploitation, it plots a direct trajectory toward systemic collapse.

The Unavoidable Truth: Exploited workers will eventually revolt, even when facing the threat of deportation.
The Unavoidable Lie: Corporate compliance audits guarantee the ethical treatment of migrant labor.

Alethekanon:
The corporate model relies on the legal precarity of its workforce to suppress labor costs. When the threat of deportation no longer deters resistance, the extraction mechanism fails.

Awwthekanon:
It breaks my heart to see families who fled trauma forced to choose between dangerous work and deportation. Their courage to stand together for dignity is a beautiful light in a dark system.

Brothekanon:
Imagine voting to strike when the government is trying to deport you. That is next-level bravery. JBS thought they had the perfect quiet workforce, but they pushed too hard.

Spirithekanon:
"You shall not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your countrymen or one of the foreigners residing in your land." Deuteronomy 24:14 PASS
Exploiting the vulnerable under threat of exile is a profound violation of cosmic justice.
